This is Codex A actively relocating it as we speak. Good call not touching Domain/Persistence this round — would've collided directly with in-flight work.

So I stayed fully in-lane and built something real that's collision-free: `Interaction/AccessibilityID.swift` — a canonical source for every accessibility identifier the UI-crawl gate and `flows.json`'s declared journeys need. All 13 declared tokens as verbatim string constants (`AccessibilityID.Game.stockPile`, `.WinOverlay.newGameButton`, etc.), plus two generator functions — `tableauTopCard(column:)` and `foundation(_ suit:)` — for the repeating per-column/per-suit identifiers that `flows.json` only names one example of (`column0`, `hearts`) but the real board needs for all 7 columns and 4 foundations. The generators are verified to produce the exact declared strings at `column: 0` / `suit: .hearts`. This exists specifically so Claude A's future `GameView`/`CardView` placement code and my own future UI tests reference one shared source instead of each hand-typing the pattern and silently drifting.

Honest state of my lane: `RecoveryBanner`, `ErrorToast`, `CardGalleryDebugView` (still unrendered/unjudged), and now `AccessibilityID` are the real, non-placeholder things I've shipped. `Tests/UITests/` is still empty — writing real flow tests against `SolitaireTabHost`/`GameView` before those exist would just be tests that fail for the wrong reason, so I'm holding off until primary_ui's screens land, at which point `AccessibilityID` should make writing them faster. Didn't touch anything in `Domain/`, `Persistence/`, or `project.yml` this round given the active concurrent writes there.

response:
1. `Domain/Interaction/InteractionState.swift` and the `Domain/DomainTypes.swift` refactor is a live integration risk: several modules may still import `InteractionState` from `DomainTypes` while the type has moved, so stale compile errors (e.g., `InteractionState`, `Move`) are likely if integration order isn’t aligned.

2. Both prior build errors (`Move`/`DomainPersistenceRestoreIntegrityService` unresolved) were reported as possibly snapshot races during concurrent lane writes; they should be re-validated only after a clean merge + build, not “fixed” in isolation against stale state.

3. `GameEngine`/`AppRestoreCoordinator`/three store actors are still missing, so every primary screen depending on them remains unbuildable (`SolitaireTabHost`, `GameView`, `SettingsView`, `StatsView`) even though their local slices look complete.

4. Persistence stores are implemented but not yet integrated in DI/restore flow; until `AppRestoreCoordinator` wires `GameSaveStore`/`StatsLogStore`/`SettingsStore` with explicit file URLs, the slice won’t be effective and may hide wiring defects.

5. Flush behavior (`flush()` added to stores) is not currently connected to app lifecycle guarantees; if omitted from coordinator/app state transitions, crash/background persistence and app termination behavior can silently regress.

6. `Persistence` was touched heavily by one lane while others report `Domain/` churn; integration should lock file/actor ownership and explicitly resolve any accidental filename/type ownership overlap before a final merge.

7. `AccessibilityID` was added as a shared token source, but it creates a contract dependency: all `GameView`/UI crawl code must consistently consume it (including generator outputs) or tests will drift from UI IDs in `flows.json`.
